text:
elaine: Quick sync — I'm running a 30min workshop tomorrow to align on the audit-event lexicon for customer-facing events and to surface any gaps between product, infra, and legal. Can folks from RBAC, KMS, and product join?

nora: I'll be there. should we include concrete examples of the event payloads so compliance can sign off? :white_check_mark:

ashwin: +1. Also want to confirm how we map internal actor types to customer-facing actor labels (eg. service-account -> 'system', delegated-actor -> 'admin') — we had some mismatches in the last export.

sam: I can bring the current product list of events we mark as "customer_visible": true. there's a short list of ~12 events we currently expose.

elaine: Perfect. goal is threefold: 1) agree on naming conventions (verb/action vs noun), 2) define minimal schema for customer-facing events, and 3) decide which internal fields to redact or transform before export.

ashwin: For naming conv, proposal: use action.verb + subject.namespace, e.g. `user.login` or `key.rotate`. avoids long sentences.

nora: I like action.verb. But product wants human-friendly labels for UI. Proposal: event.name = canonical (machine) and event.display_name = human. That way we keep both.

elaine: That matches what legal suggested — canonical name is what downstream systems (SIEMs, customers) use. display_name is OK for docs/console.

sec-bot: [automated] New RFC draft uploaded: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/286-audit-lexicon-draft (authors: elaine, ashwin)

sam: Thanks. quick question about KMS: when a key rotation happens we currently emit `key.rotate.internal` with kms_key_id and rotated_by. Customers should get `key.rotate` with only key_alias and rotation_initiator_type. Are we comfortable with that transform?

ashwin: yes but add provenance: provenance.source = "redwood-kms" and provenance.request_id for troubleshooting. provenance fields should be allowed but redacted in public exports if they contain internal ids.

nora: On redaction — we need to be explicit in schema: fields that are PII, internal_identifiers, or ephemeral tokens. Example JSON in workshop:

```
{
  "event.name": "key.rotate",
  "event.display_name": "Key rotation",
  "timestamp": "2026-03-19T16:12:05Z",
  "actor": { "type": "admin", "id": "REDACTED" },
  "resource": { "type": "kms_key", "alias": "org-prod-main" },
  "provenance": { "source": "redwood-kms", "request_id": "REDACTED" }
}
```

ashwin: That example is solid. One more: for RBAC changes we currently store both old_role and new_role as role_ids. Customers should receive role names. We'll need a mapping table in the exporter and a migration plan so old exports don't break.

elaine: Good catch. We'll add a version field: audit_schema_version, and recommend semver-style bumps when we change canonical names or field types.

sam: Who owns the mapping table? product or platform?

ashwin: infra (me) will own the runtime mapping; product owns canonical role name definitions. We'll add a read-only API for translations.

nora: A compliance question: Do we allow customers to opt-in to full internal ids for debugging under NDA? That needs a controlled playback endpoint with consent flow.

elaine: Yes — propose a BYOK (bring-your-own-key) gated endpoint for that, audit-logged and admin-approved. We'll flesh out in the workshop.

ashwin: Logistics: I can demo the current exporter transform and the mapping prototype. I'll post a short recording in thread before the workshop.

sec-bot: [automated] Reminder scheduled: Workshop "Audit lexicon & exports" tomorrow 10:00-10:30 PT. Link: https://meet.redwood/internal/rooms/8

elaine: Thanks everyone. Agenda in RFC. Please add any event examples you care about to the RFC page before EOD so we can prioritize them in the session. @sam @ashwin @nora :thumbsup:

sam: added the product list. :+1:

nora: added a compliance checklist. tiny nit: include retention flags (retention_days) in schema.

elaine: Noted. See you all tomorrow.
